evidence: Word-by-word against SOURCE.txt. Replaced words: "And when you're done, come back the other way." Draft: "When you're done, make sure to come back the other way." There are exactly two differences: the opening "And" is gone, and "make sure to" is inserted before "come back". Nothing else moves: same time condition ("when you're done"), same actor (the reader, "you"), same act ("come back the other way"); no claim, condition, person or number is added, and nothing of his is dropped except the "And". The meaning SOURCE.txt asks to keep (his published guide: "...reverse the journey when you finish") is all there ("when you're done" = "when you finish", "come back the other way" = "reverse the journey"). The one nuance I weighed: "make sure to" makes the reminder a shade firmer than the bare imperative. I judge it emphasis, not a change in strength that matters: his line is already an instruction to do it (not an option), it asks the same thing of the same person at the same moment, and the section's lines already range from "feel free" to "NOT going to help you". Dropping "And" loses only the additive link to the sentence before ("If you're going to count, do it in a way that makes sense in your world."), and the sentence stands fine after it. the_change says this is Emulate's sentence (sample cm) for his line, with no put-back fix; the draft is that sentence verbatim, so the change does what it says. (The ledger lines for T14 and T15 in ADMISSION.json say the draft 'puts back' a point Emulate dropped; I cannot see any put-back in the draft and did not rely on that wording.) CONTEXT.txt holds the draft once, in the second paragraph, between "...makes sense in your world." and "(You can borrow qualities, but don't change who you are.)", and it reads right there; its straight apostrophe matches the rest of that paragraph. TELLS: I went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the draft in its context and find none PRESENT. Closest calls: T22 (coach register) - "make sure to" is a mildly coachy phrase, but the sentence carries a real step from his line, is the same plain instruction as the source, and sits among lines with stance and asides ("whatever", the parenthetical, the "soup" line); T15 (humanizer rewording) - the changes are a dropped "And" and a common phrase, not rarer words swapped in over the same structure; T02/T09/T13 - the paragraph is a run of short instructions, but that is his structure, loosened by qualifiers and asides, and the swap adds and removes no step; T26 - "come back" echoes "one way of coming back" in the first paragraph, but the echo sits in his own structure (the point announced, then the instruction) and the draft's "come back" is the source's; C02 - "the other way" leans on the journey set up by "one way of coming back" and "the world you're creating", exactly as the source's line did. The parenthetical after the draft (T17-like) is not part of this change. LINTER: "D9 follows the source order" (1/1 paragraphs) is trivially true of a one-sentence swap in place with nothing reordered, and T13/T09 are answered above; accepted. "E36/E41 heavy second person" (9.1 "you" per 100 words) matches the draft's own count, one "you're" in 11 words; the source's line has one in 9 words (11.1), so the change lowers it; the single "you're" is the time clause of a direct instruction in a section that tells the reader how to write their own induction, and the sentence has no generic scenery (E36) or reassurance-only voice (E41); accepted.
